description: Authentic verified NASA scientific reference datasets for SPACE WARS, used for offline play, testing, and rate-limit fallbacks.

donki.source: NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information)
donki.status: DEMO MODE (Verified Historic Solar Event Archive)

events.childExplanation: A massive solar storm erupted from Sunspot AR3664! It unleashed an intense burst of X-rays and ultraviolet radiation across the solar system.
events.safetyAction: Activate radiation shielding and retreat to the subterranean habitat shelter! Martian soil (regolith) blocks dangerous solar particles.
events.gameplayImpact: Radiation spikes by +45 µSv/h. Roaming astronauts must shelter within 30 seconds.

events.childTitle: Coronal Mass Ejection Traveling at 1,500 km/s!
events.childExplanation: The Sun blasted billions of tons of magnetized solar plasma into interplanetary space at over 5 million km/h!
events.safetyAction: Fold in external solar arrays to prevent electrical damage, and power down exposed rover instruments.
events.gameplayImpact: Energy generation drops by 40%. Auxiliary batteries and RTG power must be engaged.

events.childExplanation: Super-fast protons accelerated by solar flare magnetic fields are flying through deep space near the speed of light!
events.safetyAction: Deploy heavy water-ice shields around sleeping quarters. Water hydrogen atoms absorb high-speed protons.
events.gameplayImpact: Astronaut radiation exposure risk triples if outside the shielded bunker.

events.childExplanation: Trapped particles around planets become energized during geomagnetic storms, creating intense electron belts.
events.safetyAction: Trajectory calculations must route spacecraft quickly through radiation belts to minimize crew exposure.
events.gameplayImpact: Navigation challenge: steer spacecraft along low-flux polar corridors.

events.source: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center / NASA DONKI
events.childExplanation: The most intense space storm in 20 years! On Earth it sparked global auroras. On Mars, where there is no planetary magnetosphere, the radiation reaches the surface.
events.safetyAction: All surface rovers must return to docking stations immediately.
events.gameplayImpact: Full base emergency mode: radio communications experience total solar blackout.

events.childExplanation: A coronal hole on the Sun is blowing a high-speed gust of solar wind across planetary orbits.
events.safetyAction: Align communication high-gain dish to overcome solar wind plasma interference.
events.gameplayImpact: Communication latency increases; fine-tune antenna tracking motors.

events.source: NASA GSFC Community Coordinated Modeling Center (CCMC)
events.childExplanation: NASA supercomputers simulated the CME wave moving through the inner solar system, predicting exact arrival at Moon and Mars.
events.safetyAction: Review the 3D spiral map to see how many hours until the plasma front reaches your outpost.
events.gameplayImpact: Gives players a 45-second strategic countdown before the storm hits.

studies.title: Spaceflight effects on the mouse retina: Histological, gene expression and epigenetic changes after flight on STS-135
studies.childFact: NASA study OSD-87 proved space radiation and zero-G affect delicate eye blood vessels. Astronauts wear gold-coated helmet visors to reflect 99% of dangerous solar UV rays!
studies.gameConnection: Astronaut Health & Helmet Optics: Inspect visor integrity.

studies.title: Plant growth and circadian rhythms in microgravity on the International Space Station
studies.childTitle: Growing Fresh Salad on the Moon and Mars!
studies.childFact: Plants do not need gravity to find 'up'—they follow blue and red LED light! Space greenhouse crops produce fresh oxygen and tasty greens like red romaine lettuce.
studies.gameConnection: Bio-Dome Greenhouse: Balance water, light, and nutrients to feed the crew.

studies.title: Human bone density maintenance and muscle mass preservation during long-duration spaceflight
studies.childFact: Because Mars has only 38% of Earth's gravity, astronaut bones can lose 1% of density each month without exercise! Astronauts use ARED vacuum-cylinder gym gear daily.
studies.gameConnection: Astronaut Fitness Gym: Complete daily workout routines to maintain Health.

studies.title: Immune system dysregulation during long-duration orbital spaceflight
studies.childFact: In space, T-cell immune responses can slow down. Clean air filters, healthy vitamins, and proper sleep keep astronaut immune systems working at peak performance.
studies.gameConnection: Medical Bay: Administer vitamin packs and air scrubbers.

studies.title: Circadian rhythm entrainment and cognitive performance using solid-state LED dynamic lighting on ISS
studies.childTitle: Good Night, Astronauts! Circadian Lighting in Space
studies.childFact: A day on Mars is 24 hours and 39 minutes (called a 'Sol'). NASA uses special blue-depleted evening lighting inside habitats so astronauts sleep soundly.
studies.gameConnection: Habitat Sleep Quarters: Adjust lighting spectrum for restful crew sleep.

records.childExplanation: Recorded by Liulin-5 aboard the ISS. Earth's magnetic bubble (magnetosphere) protects the station from most deep space cosmic rays.
Measured directly on the red planet surface! Mars has no global magnetic field, so radiation is ~2.5 times higher than inside the ISS. Thick shelters are essential.

records.instrument: Cosmic Ray Telescope for the Effects of Radiation
records.childExplanation: The Moon has no atmosphere or magnetic field. Galactic cosmic rays strike directly, requiring astronauts to build bases inside underground lava tubes or under lunar regolith berms.

shieldingFacts.why: A 1.5 to 2 meter blanket of crushed rock and sand piled over habitat domes stops almost all dangerous solar energetic particles!
Water is packed with lightweight hydrogen atoms, which bounce high-energy cosmic protons away like billiard balls!
Hydrogen-rich synthetic polymers make flexible, lightweight linings inside astronaut spacesuits and rover walls.
Heavy metals can actually produce secondary radiation when hit by cosmic rays. Layering with hydrogenous materials is much safer!

marstrek.source: NASA Mars Trek / Solar System Treks (USGS / JPL)
marstrek.layer: Mars MGS MOLA Color Shaded Relief Merge (463m)
marstrek.description: High resolution topographic map layer from the Mars Global Surveyor Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA).

landmarks.name: Jezero Crater
landmarks.childDescription: Billions of years ago, Jezero was filled with liquid water! Perseverance searches here for ancient microbial fossils and signs of ancient Martian life.

landmarks.name: Olympus Mons
landmarks.childDescription: The biggest volcano in the whole solar system! It is 22 kilometers high—three times taller than Mount Everest on Earth!

landmarks.name: Valles Marineris
landmarks.childDescription: A gigantic canyon system spanning over 4,000 kilometers! If placed on Earth, it would stretch all the way across North America.

landmarks.name: Gale Crater & Mount Sharp
landmarks.childDescription: Curiosity has been climbing Mount Sharp inside Gale Crater for over 12 years, discovering rounded pebbles that formed in ancient rushing river streams!

landmarks.name: Arcadia Planitia
landmarks.childDescription: A smooth northern plain with vast sheets of pure water ice buried just centimeters below the red dust—ideal for future human base water extraction!

landmarks.name: Shackleton Crater (Moon South Pole)
landmarks.feature: Lunar Ice Trap & Peak of Eternal Light
landmarks.childDescription: At the Moon's South Pole! Deep inside its dark rim lie billions of kilograms of water ice frozen for eons, while its rim receives continuous solar power.
